media.notes: 64 blocks of 8 bytes, accessed via generic GBA EEPROM bit-serial protocol over DMA3 (0x040000D4 / MMIO 0xD000000). Every 8-byte block is stored byte-reversed in the raw .sav file relative to the logical/RAM byte order used by the save code; this reversal is proven in SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.

slots_and_copies.name: identity_header
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: fixed location, blocks 0-2, written every save by FUN_0805dac4

slots_and_copies.name: settings_block
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: fixed location, block 4, part of the sparse table tail-loop in FUN_0805dac4

slots_and_copies.name: stats_slot_record
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: fixed location, blocks 56-63; only populated record observed in the otherwise-blank blocks 3-63 table; no second on-disk copy found, so file-level mirroring is unproven

checksums.name: identity_header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: checksum = sum(logical_bytes[0:20]) accumulated unmodulo'd into a 32-bit register; stored little-endian at logical offset 0x14-0x17

io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3 bit-serial transfer primitive used for both sending command/address/data bits to 0xD000000 and clocking response bits back from it; busy-waits on a ready flag before dispatching through an unresolved jump table.
DMA3 arm/trigger helper; only called from the EEPROM write path, right after the write bitstream is queued.
DMA3 disarm/cleanup helper; matching teardown for 0x0805efc8.

Reads one 8-byte EEPROM block at a given 6-bit block address; builds request bitstream, clocks 68 response bits, unpacks the last 4 16-bit words in reverse word order into the output buffer (root cause of the raw-file byte reversal).
Writes one 8-byte EEPROM block at a given 6-bit block address; builds write-opcode+data+address bitstream MSB-first, arms/polls/disarms DMA, returns status.
Read-back verify: reads the block just written via 0x0805f114 and compares all 4 words against the expected buffer; returns 0x8000 on mismatch.

Top of the hardware I/O driver actually called by game/record logic (lines 6998 and 7076 of decompiled.c, located by address cross-reference since callgraph.json does not record these callers). Retries write+verify up to 3 times.

Reads block_count EEPROM blocks via 0x0805f114, computes sum32 checksum over bytes[0,len-4) and compares to the trailing 4 bytes of the read blob, optionally copies the blob to an out buffer. Returns 0 (valid), 0x3000 (checksum mismatch), or 0x5000 (block_count out of range).

Builds a 20-byte ASCII tag + appends sum32 checksum, reads existing on-disk data via 0x0805d834 for a dirty-check, skips the physical write if unchanged, otherwise writes every block via 0x0805f2f8 with IRQs disabled.

Builds the identity tag from global name/code/revision tables, writes it via 0x0805d94c(buf,0,3), then loops writing blocks 3..N directly via 0x0805f2f8 with no per-block checksum. No caller found in the 175-function trace or callgraph.json -- top of the traceable chain.

Boot/load-time counterpart: rebuilds the expected 20-byte tag from live globals, reads the stored header via 0x0805d834(0,0,3), and flags a mismatch if the live tag or its checksum differ from what's stored.

caller_chains.trigger_context: UNKNOWN - no caller of 0x0805dac4 present in the 175-function trace or callgraph.json; gameplay trigger (level clear, menu save, etc.) not determined
caller_chains.how_mapped: Located by grepping decompiled.c for call sites of the MMIO-seed cluster (0x0805f2f8 at line 6998), then walking the single caller edge recorded by callgraph.json (0x0805d94c -> 0x0805dac4) and cross-checking against the byte-reversed logical bytes of saves/cap-01-future-1.sav, which exactly match the 20-byte tag format constructed in 0x0805dac4/0x0805d94c.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Same save event as above; tail loop of 0x0805dac4 writing blocks 3..N (per-block, uncheck-summed) of a sparse table that only has data in blocks 56-63 in both observed samples
caller_chains.how_mapped: Located via decompiled.c line 7076 (func_0x0805f2f8 call inside 0x0805dac4's for-loop); field offsets within the record identified by diffing the byte-reversed logical view of cap-00-future-0.sav vs cap-01-future-1.sav.

fields.name: identity_tag_ascii
fields.update_mechanism: Written verbatim every save by 0x0805dac4 from fixed global tables
fields.evidence: Byte-reversing logical blocks 0-2 of cap-01-future-1.sav yields readable ASCII matching the ROM's own game code (ABDP) echoed back; cap-00 shows the EEPROM-erased 0xFF sentinel, consistent with not-yet-written

fields.name: identity_tag_checksum
fields.update_mechanism: sum(logical_bytes[0:20]) recomputed and written every save
fields.evidence: Python verification: computed sum exactly equals stored value in cap-01-future-1.sav (0x41f == 0x41f); see SAVE-FORMAT-REPORT.md section 4.3

fields.name: settings_pair_0x20
fields.update_mechanism: unknown; unchanged across the only 2 samples available

fuzzing_targets.mutation: replace '/ABDP-00' tag with a fictitious game code, checksum repaired
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If 0x0805d70c's tag compare gates loading, the game should treat the save as foreign/incompatible and reinitialize rather than resume

fuzzing_targets.mutation: flip one bit of the stored checksum, leave tag bytes intact
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: 0x0805d834's checksum compare should report mismatch (0x3000); observe whether any caller actually consumes that status
If this is a lives/retries counter, 0 should produce a near-game-over state on load and 99 should allow many failures; no change falsifies the hypothesis
If this selects the resumed level, the next load should resume at an early level instead of wherever cap-01 was captured
If this is a displayed score/progress value, the stats/results screen should reflect the new value; a crash or visible clamp would indicate a narrower field width or a display-only read elsewhere

fuzzing_targets.mutation: diverge from offset 32/34 values instead of matching them
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If this is a save-time snapshot only, divergence should have no load-time effect (only re-read/overwritten at next save)

fuzzing_targets.mutation: write a non-zero, non-0xFF byte pattern into an otherwise-unwritten table block (logical 0x38-0x3F)
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Probes whether the game scans/validates this sparse table region on load; expect either silent ignore or a corrupt-entry handling path

open_questions: What concrete game-logic function calls 0x0805dac4 / supplies the src_buf to 0x0805d94c, and what gameplay trigger invokes it? Not present in the 175-function trace or callgraph.json.
Is the 0x1C0-0x1FF region a single 'current stats' record, or one live entry within a larger high-score/level table whose other slots (0x38-0x1BF) are simply unused so far?
Does 0x0805d70c's tag/checksum mismatch actually gate save loading, or is it diagnostic-only? Requires runtime tracing or the fuzzing plan.
Are the static bytes at 0x1D8-0x1EF genuinely fixed level-geometry constants, or merely static so far across 2 samples of the same level?

Why do stats_counter_a (0x1C0) and stats_counter_b (0x1CC) both increment by 1 per save but start from different values (0 vs 1)? More samples needed to determine if they are independent counters or a misread 8-byte value.
